subject: Recap & next steps — DepFast LLM API unlock plan
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Liam Carter <liam.carter@depfast.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-16T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Recap & next steps — DepFast LLM API unlock plan

Hi Liam —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth: 

Pain points (what you shared)
- Monthly spend on OpenAI + Anthropic has grown unpredictably (~$70k / mo forecast; heavy 1:1 chat usage).
- Vendor lock-in and difficulty standing up comparable infra when needed (latency and token-usage patterns).
- Need to preserve prompt templates and scoring logic (reranking + safety checks).
- Security: SOC 2 posture required, and data residency for some EU customers.

Current stack (what you described)
- Primary generation via OpenAI Chat API (GPT-4 / gpt-4o-beta for high-value flows).
- Anthropic for experimental safety-sensitive pipelines.
- In-house embedding store (Postgres + FAISS); orchestration in Kubernetes.
- Approx usage: ~2M input+output tokens/day, peak traffic during biz hours (~250 rps aggregated).

Success criteria for evaluating an open-model migration
- Quality: <= 5% drop in end-to-end task accuracy on your eval set (we'll run evals using your prompt set).
- Latency: 99th percentile < 500ms for your targeted routes (chat-short + chat-long).
- Cost: target ~30% reduction in per-token spend at equivalent QoS.
- Operational: minimal changes to client-side SDKs and ability to fallback to hosted APIs.

Initial model shortlist (compatibility-focused):
- Llama 2 (13B) — good instruction-following baseline and widely vetted.
- Mistral-Instruct (7B) — strong cost/quality tradeoff for conversational tasks.
- Falcon 40B (quantized variant) — candidate for higher-quality flows if GPU budget permits.

Proposed next steps (we recommend):
1) You share a redacted sample prompt set + small eval corpus (10–20 representative queries) — I attached sample_prompt_set.csv for format.
2) Redwood runs a 2-week PoC on Dedicated capacity with a canary route for 10% of traffic (we'll measure latency, quality, and cost).
3) Security intake: if okay, your security contact can start the SOC 2 questionnaire.
4) Align on timeline and PO/contract path — Ben (cc'd) will share a POC scope doc and checklist.

Attachments: DepFast_discovery_notes.pdf (notes from call), sample_prompt_set.csv

Would you be able to share the eval set and a rough availability window for a kickoff call next week?

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0142

Redwood Inference — production-first inference platform (hosted / dedicated / private)

From: Liam Carter <liam.carter@depfast.io>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Nisha Rao <nisha.rao@depfast.io>
Date: 2026-08-16T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps — DepFast LLM API unlock plan

Grace —

Appreciate the write-up, that aligns with what we talked about. A few clarifications / asks from our side: 

- Usage numbers: our 2M token/day is a steady-state average; bursts can double traffic for short periods during promotions.
- Latency: our internal SLO is 95th < 250ms and 99th < 500ms for customer-facing chat. Anything above that causes user complaints.
- Prompt templates: we need to preserve exact tokenization of some templates (templated system messages + user variables). Can Redwood preserve KV cache style behavior for incremental prompts?
- Embeddings: we use OpenAI embeddings for semantic search; interested if Redwood can support embedding generation + a way to migrate vector store without hitting rate limits.

Security: I'll loop in our security lead (security@depfast.io). They'll need a copy of your SOC 2 cert and the intake doc.

Availability: we can do a kickoff call next Tue or Wed morning PST. Tue 10–11am or Wed 9–10am PST works for our engineering + product team.

We'll share a redacted eval set by end of day Monday. Also worth noting: procurement will want a 60-day POC pricing model or a short-term trial commitment.

Thanks —
Liam
Head of Product, DepFast
liam.carter@depfast.io
+1 (650) 555-0199

Cc: Nisha Rao <nisha.rao@depfast.io>
Date: 2026-08-16T17:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps — DepFast LLM API unlock plan

Thanks for the notes, Liam. Quick responses to the questions and a proposed POC scope.

Compatibility / KV cache: Redwood's serving runtime preserves incremental decoding + KV cache semantics for most transformer variants; for tokenization-sensitive templates we'll run a controlled replay using your exact templates to validate parity before traffic routing.

Embeddings: yes — we can host generation alongside inference or proxy to your existing provider. Migration path for vector store: we recommend an export/import approach (we'll provide tooling to batch-generate embeddings at scale without triggering rate limits).

POC proposal (high level):
- Duration: 2 weeks (pilot), Dedicated pool sized to match your peak rps for the canary route.
- Scope: model baseline comparisons (Llama2-13B, Mistral-Instruct-7B, Falcon-40B quantized), latency/cost profiling, end-to-end eval on your sample set, integration checklist for embeddings + fallbacks.
- Deliverables: performance report, cost projection, recommended production config and routing policy.

I've attached POC_scope_v1.pdf and redwood_poc_checklist.md — these are a starting point; we can refine once we get your eval set.

For procurement: we can provide a 60-day POC rate card and a short-term commitment option; I'll include finance on the next thread once we have verbal OK.

Next calendar step: Grace to schedule kickoff for Tue 2026-08-18 10am PST (tentative). Liam to confirm and share security contact.

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Attachments: POC_scope_v1.pdf, redwood_poc_checklist.md
